chapter_theme: A song of the six shrines (ஆறு திருப்பதி): the poet confesses his bondage to courtesans who sell their arts and ruin young men's families, and asks for Murugan's feet; the praise names him the guru, Siva's son, and the lord abiding in all six shrines.

307.reading: The poet speaks of courtesans who cast nets with eyes like the wave-tossed sea, deceitful great sinners full of tricks, who flirt with fools, sell their arts for a price and ruin the families of young men, and calls himself the cheat and utter fool who falls on their breasts; he asks to be granted now the paired feet. The praise names Murugan son of Pasupati who bears the river, the six-faced form of grace and guru, the hero whose vel ruined the asuras and gave the gods back their city, the Sivaguru whom Brahma did not know, whom devotees on earth hold in mind, and the lord on the peacock abiding in the six shrines that are the source of all.
307.nuance: விலைமாதர்கள் ... இளைஞர்கள் குடிகேடிகள்: the courtesans sell and ruin households, so the charge is money and family, not desire alone. தலை அயன் அறியா ஒரு சிவகுருபரன்: Murugan as the teacher whom Brahma did not know recalls the Om story without naming it. சகலமும் முதலாகிய அறுபதி: the six shrines are themselves the first of all things.

source_issues: Song 307: line 8 reads நி முடனை, with a letter lost; probably நிர்மூடனை ('utter fool').
Chapter 27 is a single song under the heading ஆறு திருப்பதி.
